notes: 2026-08-29 (branches `chore/normalize-lock-npm10` #495 -> `fix/react-test-renderer-pin` #494, stacked, off master 2af5e9ef) — PINNED `react-test-renderer`, UNBLOCKING EVERY FUTURE FULL LOCK REGENERATION, plus a lock normalization the rebase uncovered. (1) THE PIN: a from-scratch resolution had stopped completing — `react-test-renderer` was declared and pinned NOWHERE, entering only as a FLOATING PEER of the two @testing-library packages (`jest-native@5.4.3` `>=16.0.0`, `react-native@13.3.3` `>=18.2.0`), so npm 10.8.2 resolving the manifests alone picked the registry's 19.2.8, whose `react@^19.2.8` peer collides with mobile's exact `react@19.2.0` → ERESOLVE. Nothing broke day-to-day because `npm ci` installs the pinned lock — the lock was holding the conflict back, exactly the registry-drift exposure #488 bought. Fixed with `"react-test-renderer": "19.2.0"` EXACT in apps/mobile devDependencies. ⚠️ WORKSPACE devDependency, NOT root `overrides`, FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON: this lock records NO `overrides` field at all, so an overrides pin leaves ZERO trace in the lock and `npm ci`'s own validator can never check it, whereas a workspace devDependency lands in `packages["apps/mobile"].devDependencies` and is checked every install. Both candidates resolved from scratch to BYTE-IDENTICAL trees apart from that one manifest line, so the choice was free. Bump the pin WITH mobile's `react` and jest-expo's pin (verified jest-expo@55.0.22 still declares react-test-renderer 19.2.0 exactly) — same discipline as `expo-modules-core`. NEVER `--legacy-peer-deps`. ⚠️ MEASURED: retiring `@testing-library/jest-native` does NOT free the pin — react-native@13.3.3 carries its own NON-optional `react-test-renderer >=18.2.0` peer (peerDependenciesMeta marks only `jest` optional); from-scratch across four cases: both TL packages+no pin → ERESOLVE, jest-native removed+no pin → STILL ERESOLVE, both TL removed+no pin → resolves, pin present → resolves. THE PIN STAYS. (2) THE NORMALIZATION (#495, lock-only, landed first): rebasing revealed the documented regen recipe is no longer a no-op on master — #485 (dependabot) regenerated the lock with an npm outside our 10.8.2 rule, introducing `libc` (4 lightningcss musl/glibc entries) and inflating `devOptional` 139→296 (libc=0/devOptional=139 held from 87ae7ea5 through ecfd8efb; changed at 424c7201). Control test: master's manifests+lock UNCHANGED under `npx -y npm@10.8.2 install --package-lock-only` rewrites 354 lines. Local npm 11.9.0 doesn't reproduce master's shape either (strips libc, keeps devOptional 296) — a THIRD npm wrote it. Normalization proven package-neutral entry-by-entry: 2637→2637 entries, key sets identical, version diffs 0, integrity diffs 0, resolved diffs 0; only devOptional(157)/dev(185)/libc(4) fields differ. Split into its own PR so a repo-wide lock rewrite isn't buried in a one-line pin; #494 then collapses to its genuine 1 lock line. ⚠️ `npm run verify` was 18/18 FULL TURBO CACHED on the lock change — meaningless as a gate; real greens came from direct `npx jest`: api 180 suites/3130 tests, mobile 90/1242. Open follow-up (chip task_a93e4f99): npm 10 records no `libc`, prod is node:20-alpine (musl) — unproven whether npm 10 can mis-select a glibc lightningcss binary; pre-existing, both lock shapes have deployed SUCCESS.
